overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: staff emails and separate calls by the Executive Secretary were not a quorum deliberation, and the public-input allegation was declined as outside the OML.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board deliberated outside a posted meeting about a traffic study submitted with a cannabis business application, then approved it after minimal discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Because a quorum of the Board did not communicate on a matter within the Board’s jurisdiction outside of a posted meeting, either contemporaneously or serially, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Emails about the traffic study went to Board members from staff and consultants; the complaint treated them as deliberation, and the Executive Secretary's separate calls to members were also reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: As all the emails we reviewed were sent by non-Board members to the Board, and the attached documents did not contain the opinions of any Board member, we find that these emails did not constitute deliberation in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not let the public give input on the traffic study results. The AG declined to review because the OML does not require public participation.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body allow public participation during its meetings.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
